market_narrative.headline: Fed/rates keeps risk appetite mixed and wait-and-see as investors await confirmation
market_narrative.summary: US equities are carrying a mixed and wait-and-see bias as Fed/rates, oil/energy, inflation shape positioning. Investors are balancing selective leadership against the risk that policy, rates or growth data broadens the pressure.

key_forces.label: Negative driver
key_forces.text: Headline and policy uncertainty keep the risk premium elevated

key_forces.label: Main theme
key_forces.text: Positioning is waiting for confirmation from Treasury yields, breadth and whether leadership broadens

watch_next: Treasury yields, breadth and whether leadership broadens

index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (197), inflation (135), oil/energy (100), growth/jobs (43). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is mixed and wait-and-see: 263 positive, 307 negative, and 1261 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.

themes.current_view: Fed policy is still restrictive, but investors are watching whether softer data pulls rate-cut expectations forward.
